en: Mayon Volcano has steep slopes because its highly viscous lava cools and hardens quickly before flowing far.
Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant generates electricity because underground magma heats groundwater into steam that spins turbines.
Baguio City experiences cooler temperatures than Manila because its high elevation causes the atmospheric air to expand and cool.
The Puerto Princesa Underground River formed because slightly acidic rainwater slowly dissolved the soluble limestone bedrock over millions of years.
Tubbataha Reef corals bleach and turn white when unusually warm sea temperatures cause them to expel their symbiotic algae.
The Chocolate Hills turn brown during the dry season because the lack of rainfall dries out the grass covering them.
Cagayan River frequently overflows because heavy rainfall in the surrounding Sierra Madre mountains causes rapid water runoff into the channel.
The Banaue Rice Terraces prevent soil erosion because their stepped stone walls slow down water runoff on steep mountain slopes.
Taal Volcano produces violent explosions when rising hot magma contacts the cool water of Taal Lake, creating sudden steam expansion.
The Sierra Madre mountain range protects Luzon from severe typhoon damage because its dense forests absorb heavy rain and slow strong winds.
The Verde Island Passage has strong ocean currents because its narrow strait shape forces large volumes of water to flow faster.
Laguna de Bay suffers from algal blooms because excess agricultural fertilizers wash into the shallow lake and provide nutrients for rapid algae growth.
